content: 1. All individuals diagnosed with diabetes should be encouraged to actively participate in Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support (DSMES) programs. These programs are designed to enhance their ability to make informed decisions, adopt effective self-care behaviors, solve problems related to their condition, and collaborate effectively with their healthcare teams. 2. 3. The primary objectives of DSMES include improving clinical outcomes, enhancing overall health status, and promoting well-being. These outcomes should be routinely assessed as part of comprehensive diabetes care. 4. DSMES programs must be culturally sensitive and tailored to align with the individual preferences, needs, and values of each patient. These programs can be delivered in either group settings or one-on-one sessions. Additionally, the education and support provided should be thoroughly documented and made accessible to the entire diabetes care team. 5. To overcome barriers to access and improve patient satisfaction, DSMES should be considered for delivery through telehealth services or digital platforms. 6. It is recommended that third-party payers provide reimbursement for DSMES, as evidence demonstrates that these programs lead to improved health outcomes and reduced healthcare costs. 7. Barriers to DSMES should be identified and addressed at multiple levels, including those related to payers, healthcare systems, clinics, healthcare professionals, and individual patients. 8.
